card.intuition: A system that systematically fetches web pages, extracts links, and enqueues new URLs — starting from seed URLs and traversing the web graph until it can rediscover everything. A URL frontier controls which pages to fetch next, a seen-set dedupes visits, and politeness rules throttle how fast hosts are hammered.
card.analogy: A tireless librarian who starts with a handful of books, reads each, notes the books its citations point to, and adds those to her reading pile — while making sure she never reads the same book twice and doesn't storm the same shelf too often.
card.time_complexity: Each page requires one fetch plus O(1) link extraction and dedup check; total cost scales with the number of pages crawled.
card.space_complexity: The URL frontier and seen-set grow with the count of distinct discovered URLs, which can be billions for the whole web.
when_to_use: Building a search-engine index or a data pipeline over many websites
Monitoring sites for changes or capturing content at scale
Collecting large datasets from distributed sources
gotchas: Politeness matters: fetching too fast from one host gets you blocked and violates robots.txt expectations
The crawl frontier must dedupe aggressively, or the same page gets crawled repeatedly and wastes bandwidth
Crawling is I/O-bound and highly concurrent — you need careful throttling and graceful retries

steps.annotation: Seed URLs seed the priority frontier that decides what to fetch next.
A pool of fetchers downloads pages, respecting per-host politeness limits.
The parser extracts outbound links and page content.
Links are deduped against the seen-set; new URLs are enqueued to the frontier.
Raw pages and queued URLs persist so the crawl can resume across failures.

exercise.prompt: A crawler fetches 10 pages from host A every 60 seconds to be polite. How many requests per second does it allow to that host?
exercise.starter_code:
pages = 10
seconds = 60

requests_per_second = pages / seconds
# Result is ___ requests/second
hints: Divide the number of pages by the time window
exercise.test_code:
def check(ans):
    try: return round(float(ans),2) == 0.17
    except: return False
assert check("0.1667")
print("PASS")
